previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for recurrent epistaxis and acute posthemorrhagic anemia following a hypotensive episode in the emergency department. He had a 10-point hematocrit drop over several months with dark stools and recent weight loss. He received three units of packed red blood cells, with hemoglobin stabilization after the third unit. His warfarin was slightly reduced, and Plavix remained on hold. The nosebleed resolved with conservative management. Mild hyponatremia and hypovolemia, likely due to diuresis and blood loss, resolved. He was evaluated for deconditioning and declined inpatient rehabilitation; home health services and family support were arranged. A GI workup for possible upper GI bleeding and weight loss was planned for outpatient follow-up with his PCP. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor weight, continue nasal saline, and follow up for INR and CBC testing.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF SYNOPSIS:
___ yo man with a PMH significant for DMII, COPD, and CHF who 
presents with dizziness, shortness of breath, and 55 lb weight 
loss over the past ___ years.  In short, he was initially admitted 
for dizziness that was found to be due to hypovolemia.  There 
was concern over recent weight loss, numerous elevated 
inflammatory and auto-immune markers, evidence of liver injury, 
myalgias, and marked dyspnea without hypoxia or 
PFTs/radiological consistent with significant COPD, and thus 
work-up was made for underlying rheumatologic, hematologic, or 
primary pulmonary disorder leading to this patient's recurrent 
hospitalizations, usually attributed to COPD and CHF.  In 
consultation with various inpatient services, we have made a 
preliminary diagnosis of amiodarone toxicity resulting in 
multisystem injury and have stopped this medication after 
discussion with his cardiologist.  He will require close 
follow-up as an outpatient in order to monitor his recovery and 
confirm this diagnosis.
.
OUTSTANDING ISSUES FOR PATIENT (ACTION REQUIRED):
Patient should attend the following appointments: 
.

discuss making a dermatology follow-up for plaque-like rash 
noted on his scalp
.

.

lung injury with PFTs, evaluate chest CAT scan, and to determine

.

positive lab result
.
--___ at 1 ___ with Dr. ___.  Cardiology 
follow-up now that amiodarone is stopped.
.
The most notable medication changes for this patient were:
------STOP amiodarone
------STOP Lipitor
------20 mg prednisone PO BID for 5 days, 20 mg prednisone PO QD 
for 5 days
.
DETAILED COURSE:
# Dizziness: The patient was orthostatic in the ED and was given 
fluids overnight. Both his orthostasis and dizziness resolved by 
the morning.  Thus, his initial presentation of dizziness was 
attributed to dehydration, especially in light of a recent 
increase of his furosemide dosage from 40 to 60 mg/day in 
setting of a prior CHF exacerbation.
.
# Chest pain and dyspnea:
The patient was ruled out for MI with normal ECG and negative 
troponins.  He was ruled out for stroke with negative head CT 
and reassuring neurologic exam in consultation with Neurology.  
His chest pain was bilateral and varied with position.  
According to the patient, he had been having this pain 
intermittently for the past two months.  The etiology of his 
dyspnea was likely multifactorial.  He was never hypoxic during 
his hospitalization and had relatively clear XR. PFTs were 
performed and the results were actually restrictive in nature 
which was surprising as he carried a diagnosis of COPD.  There 
was significant decrease in FEV1 and FVC compared to ___ years 
ago.  In addition, his DLCO was decreased.  This is consistent 
with either CHF or interstitial lung disease, although the 
marked decrease in DLCO is less consistent with CHF.  Further 
his exam was never suggestive of volume overload with the 
exception of some mild pulmonary infiltrate, so we believe there 
may be a component of early amiodarone lung toxicity.  He had a 
slight obstructive component consistent with his COPD as his FVC 
improved with bronchodilators.  The patient had a recent chest 
CT from ___ that showed no lung fibrosis, but we think there 
is significant laboratory data (see below) to support amiodarone 
toxicity as an explanation for his lung injury.  Thus we have 
stopped his amiodarone.  On recommendations from pulmonology, he 
was discharged with a short course of pulsed steroids to improve 
his obstructive component, Advair, and tiotropium.  He has 
follow-up chest CT scheduled for next week with pulmonology 
follow-up.
.  
# ___ positive, elevated ESR/CRP, hypergammaglobulinemia: Pt 
presented initially with elevated CK, hyperkalemia, and 
myoglobulinuria.  This resolved over the course of three days 
with gentle fluids, and there was no clear etiology.  CK trended 
down and was not high enough to favor rhabdomyolysis.  We noted 
that he was hospitalized for a similar episode ___ years prior 
(elevated CK, muscle pain, abnormal EMG).  In addition the 
patient was found to have low titers ___ and SMA antibodies, 
elevated ESR/CRP, and we have data from his outpatient PCP 
indicated hypergammaglobulinemia.  Given his weight loss, a low 
grade fever, pulmonary complaints, and myalgias, we performed 
lab tests to rule out HIV, TB, rheumatoid arthritis, 
sarcoidosis.  He was up to date for age appropriate cancer 
screening and had normal outpatient TSH. Rheum was consulted and 
felt myositis and SLE unlikely, although they suggested 
possibility of polymyalgia rheumatica.  Hematology/oncology also 
weighed in, and felt blood smear not consistent with primary 
hematologic malignancy and labs did not indicate neoplastic 
plasma cell dyscrasia.  Statin myopathy was possible explanation 
for elevated CK and myalgias, and thus atorvastatin was stopped, 
with expectation that PCP or other provider would restart with 
another statin like pravastatin.  Etiology of these lab 
abnormalities are still unclear, but many of the most concerning 
diagnoses were ruled out during this hospitalization.
.  
# Chronic transaminitis, hypoalbuminemia, SMA positive: GGT 
elevation confirms this is due to liver, and abdominal 
ultrasound confirmed fatty change.  SMA titers appeared low for 
autoimmune hepatitis, but we will have him see an outpatient 
hepatologist.  Amiodarone causes AST/ALT elevations in ___ of 
patients, and is known to progress to hepatitis/cirrhosis.  He 
has been on amiodarone as long as he has had transaminitis (more 
than 8 months), and our intervention was stopping the amiodarone 
and the atorvastatin.  Patient was negative for viral hepatitis 
labs.
.
# Peripheral eosinophilia: The absolute eosinophil count was 
persistent above 500.  Unusual to have eosinophilia rather than 
eosinopenia in setting of stress.  We had no history concerning 
for infection.  Given systemic symptoms, we ruled out Addison's 
___ and Churg ___. We noted that amiodarone is associated 
with a peripheral eosinophilia and expect this to resolve with 
stopping the medication.
.
# Anemia: The patient had a normocytic, normochromic anemia with 
normal iron labs and a low retic index of 1.1%, which was 
consistent with an inflammatory block due another underlying 
process.  The patient had some labs consistent with hemolytic 
anemia but this was likely due to his mechanical aortic valve 
replacement, and smear showed no schistocytes.
.  
INACTIVE ISSUES
.
# s/p CVA: The patient was continued on aspirin and coumadin
.  
# CAD: The patient's statin was held in light of possible statin 
myopathy.  We recommend restarting statin therapy with an agent 
like pravastatin once his current symptoms fully resolve.  
Aspirin and metoprolol were continued.
.  
# diastolic/systolic CHF (EF 45%): The patient was fluid 
resuscitated on his first evening, but was consistently diuresed 
for >500 cc/day following this.  He appeared euvolemic on exam 
and imaging throughout his hospitalization.
.  
# DM:  
Patient was kept on a humalog insulin sliding scale.
.  
# AVR/arrhythmia: Patient was continued on coumadin with INR 
range 2.5-3.5 given mechanical valve.

At the time of discharge his vital signs were stable, he was 
tolerating a regular diet, he was ambulating well and his 
follow-up appointments were set-up.

Discharge Instructions:
It was a privilege to care for you this past week at the ___ 
___.

You were admitted to the general medicine service with 
dizziness, shortness of breath, and chest pain.  We found no 
evidence for any dangerous heart problems, and we found that the 
cause of your dizziness was dehydration, possibly due to your 
recently increased water pill (Lasix) dosage.  Your dizziness 
resolved with fluids, and we will return you to your original 
dosage of Lasix at 40 mg/day.

We were concerned by your significant weight loss, loss of 
appettite, and recurring pain in your chest and legs.  Because 
you felt so short of breath, we ran many tests to try to find a 
cause of your symptoms.  We have evidence that some of your 
recent health issues may be due to the longterm effects of 
amiodarone, a drug that you take to preserve your heart rhythm.  
Speaking with your cardiologist Dr. ___ our inpatient 
specialists, we decided to take you off this medication.  We 
will also stop your Lipitor for now as it may have contributed 
to some of your symptoms.  If we are correct, you should start 
to slowly feel better with regards to your breathing over the 
course of many months.

The pulmonologists (lung specialists) evaluated you while you 
were here, and have recommended that you take prednisone for 
your shortness of breath.  They would also like for you to get a 
CT chest for evaluation of possible amiodarone toxicity or other 
lung disease that could cause your symptoms.

MEDICATION CHANGES:
*Please STOP taking amiodarone
*Please STOP taking Lipitor (atorvastatin)
*Please STOP your fluticasone inhaler
*START prednisone.  You will take 20mg of prednisone twice a day 
for five days, and then 20mg of prednisone daily for 5 days.
*Start Tiotropium 18 mcg Capsule, w/ Inhalation, once per day
*Start Advair twice per day.  You can discuss with Dr. ___ 
when to stop this.

It will be important for you to follow-up with the doctors 
listed below in the coming weeks, as our plan for your care will 
continue outside of the hospital as well.  We believe that under 
their care your health will continue to improve over time.

brain.  5  mm soft tissue and 2.5 mm bone kernel images were generated in the

age-related involutional changes.  Periventricular white matter hypodensities
are consistent with small vessel ischemic disease.  Calcifications are noted
in the cavernous and supraclinoid portions of the internal carotid arteries,
as well as the right vertebral artery.  There is stable dolichoectasia of the
right vertebral artery.  There is no shift of the normally midline structures.
The basal cisterns are patent.

Mild mucosal thickening is noted throughout the ethmoid air cells.  The
remaining paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial pathological process.
2.  CCerebral atrophy.

ADDENDUM AT ATTENDING REVIEW: If not contraindicated, MRI scanning is more
sensitive than CT imaging in detecting acute brain ischemia, particularly in
the posterior fossa (which could relate to the stated symptom of dizziness).
